facts.text: Rooms by the night, no questions
facts.why: Stock sign wording that makes the Taft sound like a no-questions motel. In the film the Taft is a smart hotel where the staff come to know and greet Ben as Mr. Gladstone (Wikipedia). No page I opened shows the check-in dialogue, so whether the clerk asks questions is unsettled, but the sign reads wrong for this hotel.

notes: Writer's doubt settled: the card still (Ben in herringbone tweed, Mrs. Robinson in a big cheetah print coat) is the Taft Hotel: 'Mrs. Robinson shows up at the infamous Taft Hotel in a large cheetah print coat' (Frankly My Dear) and Bamf Style places that tweed at the Taft lounge meeting before the first tryst. So the 'THE TAFT HOTEL' label is right. Gladstone, the drive-in, the pool, McGuire's one word, the car running dry short of the Santa Barbara church and the bus all match Wikipedia; note quote verbatim. 1967 stamps match the story.

vibe.verdict: The Taft in-room menu with Mr. Gladstone and the cheetah coat still is a smart frame, but the dishes are stock hotel food and the writing is flat.
missing: 'Plastics.' printed as Mr. McGuire's word (graduation party)
Ben in the scuba suit at the bottom of the pool (21st birthday)
Ben and Elaine on the bus, still in her wedding dress
Mrs. Robinson's leg in the doorway (the poster shot)
ideas: Swap the prawn cocktail note 'Mr. McGuire has one word for Ben.' for 'One word: plastics.'
Swap 'Drifting-in-the-pool crab and cucumber cups' note for 'Ben sits on the pool floor in a wetsuit.'
Swap the iced tea note for 'Elaine! Elaine!' with the car running dry kept in the name.
